title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 91
paragraphs: That is what happened afterwards. At the time we are speaking of, the well-to-do on Aegina overcame the common people, who had risen against them along with Nicodromus. Once they had the rebels in their power, they led them out to execution. From this came a curse which they could not expiate by any sacrifice, despite everything they tried; instead, they were driven off their island before the goddess relented. They had taken about seven hundred of the commoners prisoner, and were leading them out to die, when one of them broke free of his bonds and fled for refuge to the entrance of the temple of Demeter the Lawgiver. He seized the ring of the door and clung to it; and when they found that they could not pry him loose no matter how hard they pulled, they cut off his hands and carried him off, while his hands remained clinging to the door-handle.
